_readme: Template for one GS subject. Copy it, set subject_slug, and add mega-topics > sub-topics > leaf topics. Each leaf topic needs the 5 sections, 2-8 concepts (each with 2-8 key points), 15 MCQs and at least one PYQ to be 'ready'. See docs/CONTENT_PIPELINE.md. Optional: list books under "books" and give a concept "versions" and "book_refs" (see the Preamble example); set "require_versions": true to make versions mandatory.

children.title: Preamble — Ideals and Legal Status
children.ordering_justification: The Preamble states the objectives every later topic builds on.

concepts.title: Objectives Resolution as the source of the Preamble
key_points: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946
Constituent Assembly adopted it on 22 January 1947
it laid down the philosophy that the Preamble later reflected
misconceptions: The Preamble was drafted first and the Objectives Resolution came after it

concepts.title: The five descriptions of the Indian state
key_points: India is sovereign, free of external control
socialist and secular were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976
democratic means government by the people's elected representatives
republic means the head of state is elected, not hereditary
misconceptions: Socialist and secular were in the original 1950 Preamble

versions.title: The five descriptions, in plain words

blocks.text: The Preamble calls India a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic**. Sovereign means India takes its own decisions, free of outside control. Democratic means the government is chosen by the people. Republic means the head of state is elected, not born into the job.

blocks.title: Remember
blocks.text: **Socialist** and **secular** were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. The other three words were in the original 1950 text.

versions.title: The five descriptions at a glance

terms.definition: India is free of external control.
Government is chosen by the people's elected representatives.
The head of state is elected, not hereditary.

concepts.title: Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity
key_points: justice is social, economic and political
liberty covers thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
equality means equality of status and of opportunity
fraternity assures the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation
misconceptions: Fraternity means only brotherhood between communities, not national unity

concepts.title: Legal status of the Preamble
key_points: Berubari Union case 1960 held the Preamble is not part of the Constitution
Kesavananda Bharati case 1973 held it is part of the Constitution
the Preamble is not enforceable in a court of law
it cannot override the specific provisions of the Constitution
misconceptions: Courts can enforce the Preamble directly as a fundamental right

concepts.title: Authority and adoption of the Constitution
key_points: We, the People of India are the source of the Constitution's authority
the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949
it came into force on 26 January 1950

blocks.title: Start Here
blocks.text: The Preamble is the Constitution's introduction: who gives it authority, what kind of state India is, and what it aims to achieve.
It declares India a **Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic** and sets four objectives: **Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity**.

content_sections.title: NCERT Reference — Philosophy of the Constitution

blocks.text: The chapter 'The Philosophy of the Constitution' discusses the Preamble's values.
Is the Preamble part of the Constitution?
**Berubari (1960)**: no. **Kesavananda Bharati (1973)**: yes, and it can be amended under Article 368 without destroying the basic structure. **LIC of India (1995)**: reaffirmed.

blocks.title: Write one dated news link per topic
blocks.text: Connect the topic to a recent judgment, debate or event, with its date and source.

blocks.wrong: The Preamble has never been amended.
blocks.correct: It was amended once, by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

blocks.wrong: Courts can strike down a law for violating the Preamble.
blocks.correct: The Preamble is non-justiciable; courts use it to interpret ambiguous provisions.

pyqs.question_text:
Which one of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India?
(a) Liberty of thought
(b) Economic liberty
(c) Liberty of expression
(d) Liberty of belief
pyqs.explanation: The Preamble lists liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; economic liberty is not among them.

mcq_questions.question_text: Which Constitutional Amendment added the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble?
mcq_questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'. It is the only amendment so far to the Preamble.

mcq_questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Preamble is part of the Constitution.
2. The Preamble is enforceable in a court of law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq_questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held the Preamble to be part of the Constitution, but it is non-justiciable: it is neither a source of power nor a limit on it.

mcq_questions.question_text: In which case did the Supreme Court first say that the Preamble is NOT part of the Constitution?
mcq_questions.explanation: The Berubari reference (1960) said the Preamble is not part of the Constitution; Kesavananda Bharati (1973) reversed this.

mcq_questions.question_text: The Objectives Resolution, on which the Preamble is based, was moved in the Constituent Assembly by:
mcq_questions.explanation: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946; the Assembly adopted it on 22 January 1947.

mcq_questions.question_text: According to the Preamble, the source of authority of the Constitution is:
mcq_questions.explanation: The Preamble opens with 'We, the people of India', placing authority in the people.

mcq_questions.question_text: Which date is mentioned in the Preamble?
mcq_questions.explanation: The Preamble records that the Constitution was adopted, enacted and given to ourselves on 26 November 1949. It came into force on 26 January 1950.

mcq_questions.question_text: What is the correct order of the words describing India in the Preamble?
mcq_questions.explanation: The Preamble reads 'SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC'.

mcq_questions.question_text: The ideals of justice — social, economic and political — in the Preamble are taken from:
mcq_questions.explanation: Social, economic and political justice is drawn from the Russian Revolution (1917).

mcq_questions.question_text: The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble are taken from:
mcq_questions.explanation: Liberty, equality and fraternity are the ideals of the French Revolution.

options.label: B
options.text: The head of state is elected and not hereditary

options.label: C
options.text: India has a parliamentary form of government

mcq_questions.explanation: A republic has an elected head of state; India's President is elected indirectly for a fixed term.

mcq_questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the liberties mentioned in the Preamble?
mcq_questions.explanation: The Preamble lists liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship. Economic liberty is not listed.

mcq_questions.question_text: According to the Preamble, fraternity assures:

options.label: A
options.text: The dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation

options.label: B
options.text: Equality of status and of opportunity

mcq_questions.explanation: The Preamble promotes 'FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation'.

mcq_questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Preamble can be amended under Article 368.
2. An amendment to the Preamble may alter the basic structure of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq_questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati held the Preamble can be amended under Article 368, but not so as to destroy the basic structure.

mcq_questions.question_text: In which case did the Supreme Court again hold that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution?
mcq_questions.explanation: In LIC of India (1995) the Court reaffirmed that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.

mcq_questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): The Preamble is not a source of power to the legislature.
Reason (R): The Preamble is non-justiciable.
Choose the correct answer:

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false but R is true

mcq_questions.explanation: Both are true. The Preamble gives no power because it is an introduction stating the Constitution's objectives; non-justiciability (not enforceable in court) is a separate feature, so R does not explain A.
